info.title: LoonFS HTTP API
info.description: Static OpenAPI document for the LoonFS v0 HTTP API.

get.description: Returns `ok` when the server is running and can accept requests.
Returns this process's metrics in Prometheus text exposition format 0.0.4. Unlike `/health` and `/readiness`, the route requires the deployment's bearer token.

Returns `ready` while the server admits new work. Once shutdown begins and publisher admission closes, answers 503 `shutting_down` so load balancers can drain the instance. `/health` stays the liveness probe: it only reports that the process is up.

503.description: Shutdown has begun; admission is closed

get.description: Lists every active checkpoint record on the namespace, oldest first. Each record is a garbage-collection root, and its id is what the release endpoint takes; because a checkpoint name is a label rather than a key, this is the only way to find a pin whose creation response is gone. An expired record that no collection pass has released yet is still active and is listed, with its expiry in the entry — the operator is looking for roots, and a record that still pins its basis is one. Released records are absent: a release is what stops a record pinning anything.

post.description: Creates a named, user-owned checkpoint record pinning the current namespace view. Every call mints a new record under a new id; the name is a label, not a key. The record is a garbage-collection root until it is released, so routine maintenance should flush the WAL instead. This is a maintenance/admin operation, not a file mutation.

400.description: Invalid namespace id, name, or lifetime

post.description: Releases a user-owned checkpoint pin by id. Idempotent: releasing an already-released or reaped record succeeds. The record is reaped by a later garbage-collection pass; its pinned data becomes collectable only on the pass after that.

400.description: Invalid id, or the checkpoint is fork-owned

get.description: Reports where the namespace's grep index is: `disabled`, `backfilling` with the sequence it walks toward and how far the walk got, or `steady` with the watermark it has built through. One grep root read, no side effects. A namespace that never enabled the index reads as `disabled`. Requires this deployment to maintain the grep index.

403.description: The backing store rejected its configured credentials

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not maintain the grep index

post.description: Disables the namespace's grep root and clears its segment references with one durable compare-and-swap; index maintenance stops on its own once a step reads the disabled root. Explicit grep garbage collection later reclaims the segments. Idempotent. Requires this deployment to maintain the grep index.

200.description: Grep root disabled or already disabled

403.description: The backing store rejected its configured credentials

409.description: Lost a grep root-pointer publication race; retry

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not maintain the grep index

post.description: Enables the namespace's grep root and asks this deployment's maintenance runner for the backfill's first step. The response reports the durable lifecycle it published or found: a fresh enable is `backfilling` with the sequence its checkpoint captured, while an already-enabled namespace answers with whichever phase it is in. Idempotent. Requires this deployment to maintain the grep index.

200.description: Grep root enabled or already enabled

403.description: The backing store rejected its configured credentials

409.description: Lost a grep root-pointer publication race; retry

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not maintain the grep index

post.description: Runs one explicit garbage-collection pass over only this namespace's grep-owned extension keyspace. A tombstoned or absent namespace has aged extension state reaped; no grep garbage collection runs implicitly. `max_objects` bounds the reads the pass spends and returns a `next_cursor` when keys remain; resuming re-reads liveness and the grep root, so a cursor only skips enumeration. Requires this deployment to maintain the grep index.

403.description: The backing store rejected its configured credentials

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not maintain the grep index

post.description: Runs one bounded maintenance step. The body selects the actions by naming them: `metadata` folds the WAL tail once it reaches the threshold and merges one bounded reorganization unit, `advance_retention: true` advances the retention floor, and `gc` runs one bounded garbage-collection pass. Selected actions run in that order, each reports separately, and an absent report means the body did not select that action. A body that selects nothing is rejected. Nothing surrenders replay history or sweeps objects unless the body asked for it. A deleted namespace accepts a step that selects `gc` alone, which is how its reclaimable state is collected; any other selection is refused. Step-driven GC defaults to 1024 candidates and returns its cursor for a later step rather than looping internally. Losing the root race is an outcome, not an error.

Proves the configured object store honours the create-if-absent, compare-and-swap, visibility, listing, and ranged-read semantics LoonFS depends on, and reports what it found check by check. Nothing runs this implicitly: a probe writes and deletes objects, all of them under a scratch prefix that is not a durable object family, and its last check deletes them and proves the prefix empty. A store that fails a check answers 200 with that check reported `failed` — the probe ran, and the answer is that the store is wrong. Optional capabilities a store declares it lacks answer `unsupported`, which is an answer rather than a fault. This route does not decide whether the deployment may serve presigned direct uploads: that trust comes from the endpoint allowlist, because a probe exercises the server's own request path and never a presigned capability handed to a client.

200.description: Probe completed; per-check outcomes are in the body

get.description: Returns a summary of supported features and limits.

409.description: Namespace already exists or is partial

410.description: Namespace id was deleted and retired

get.description: Returns the current head, manifest, checkpoint, WAL tail, and retention state for a namespace.

parameters.name: expected_head_seq
parameters.description: Delete only if the namespace head is still at this sequence

get.description: Returns committed changes from the write-ahead log. Callers can use this feed to keep another projection synchronized with WAL history.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Return committed changes after this sequence

post.description: Applies one commit: an ordered, non-empty list of path operations that commit together as one logical commit, under one commit id that makes retries idempotent. A single-operation call is the one-element case. The first operation that fails aborts the whole request, and a request carrying more than one operation names that operation's position in `details.operation_index`.

get.description: Returns file bytes for the current revision at a path, or for a specific retained revision when `revision_no` is provided.

404.description: Namespace, path, or revision not found

503.description: The server is at its concurrent content-read limit; retry shortly

post.description: Authorizes one direct read of a file's content object and returns a short-lived presigned GET capability, the resolved revision, and the content reference the client checks the arriving bytes against. `Range` is outside the signature, so one grant serves ranged, resumed, and parallel reads. Deployments that cannot presign answer 501 `not_supported`; the proxied `GET /filesystem/content` route stays available and is capped by `download.max_content_bytes`.

404.description: Namespace, path, or revision not found

get.description: Lists a directory at the current namespace head.

parameters.name: include_attributes
parameters.description: Project each entry's attribute map and revision (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `false`: a page holds many entries and each map may be 64 KiB, so a listing does not carry them unless asked.

400.description: Invalid path, limit, cursor, or include_attributes

get.description: Resolves the current path to a file inode and returns revisions for that file. If the file could be renamed, use the inode revision API for stable identity.
Returns the current metadata for a path, including inode identity, kind, display name, file content metadata, and the inode's attributes.

parameters.name: include_attributes
parameters.description: Project the inode's attribute map and revision (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `true`: a stat answers for one path and a map is capped at 64 KiB.

get.description: Returns the namespace's recoverable deletions, oldest deletion first. Entries never age out at the retention floor; each carries the inode id and deletion sequence undelete needs, plus the deleted name when the delete recorded one.

post.description: Creates a new namespace as a fork from the source namespace's current durable view.

Searches file content with a regular expression, accelerated by the namespace's grep index. Matches are verified against the real pattern and returned in ascending `(inode_id, byte_offset)` order; revisions committed after the index watermark are scanned exhaustively unless `allow_stale` skips them. Requires this deployment to serve grep and the namespace to carry a materialized steady-state grep root.

400.description: Invalid pattern, cursor, or an unindexable pattern without allow_scan

403.description: The backing store rejected its configured credentials

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not serve grep queries, the grep index is not enabled, or its backfill has not completed on this namespace

503.description: The index trails the head past the scan budget

post.description: Starts an upload session for content that may later be attached to a file. Service-proxied uploads send bytes through the server; direct-put uploads return object-store presigned credentials.

get.description: Reads one upload session. A completed session answers with a freshly minted validation token for its content, so a client that lost a commit response can commit again without re-uploading anything.

post.description: Ends an upload session without selecting content and deletes the object it was writing. Repeating it succeeds; a session that already completed cannot be aborted.
Completes an upload session once the caller confirms the expected content reference. The response may include a short-lived validation token for a following file write.

put.description: Uploads bytes into a service-proxied upload session and returns the content reference for the stored object.

503.description: The server is at its concurrent proxied-upload limit; retry shortly

post.description: Returns one short-lived, checksum-bound upload capability per requested part of an open direct_multipart session. Asking again for a part is how a client retries it.

AbortUploadResponse.description: Response after aborting an upload session.

aborted_at_ms.description:
Unix-millisecond stamp of the abort that stands, which for a repeated
abort is the first one's.

AbsolutePath.description: Validated complete absolute namespace path, serialized as a plain string.

ActorId.description: Opaque hosting-platform actor id: non-empty, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes, without leading or trailing whitespace or control characters.

ActorKind.description: The type of actor responsible for a commit.

ActorRef.description:
Identifies the user, service, or system responsible for a commit.

LoonFS stores this value as provided. It does not authenticate the actor or
look up profile information.

id.description: A stable identifier supplied by the application.

AdvanceRetentionResponse.description: Result of advancing the retention floor.

retention_floor_seq.description: New minimum sequence for incremental replay.

ApiError.description: HTTP error body used by LoonFS APIs.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable reason from the [`ErrorCode`](crate::ErrorCode)
registry.

Carried as a string so clients keep working when a newer server
introduces a code they do not know; use
[`ErrorCode::parse`](crate::ErrorCode::parse) for typed access.

oneOf.description:
Structured context for the code, present when the failure carries
machine-usable identity (API spec, "Standard error contract"). Boxed
so the rare detailed error does not widen every error-carrying result.

feature.description:
For `not_supported` errors, the capability-document feature key the
client should reconcile against.

request_id.description:
Correlation id the server assigned to the failed request; the same
value is sent as the `x-request-id` response header.

AttributeKey.description:
Validated name of one inode attribute.

A key is 1 to 128 UTF-8 bytes and carries no Unicode control
character, which is also what rejects NUL. Keys are compared exactly:
nothing case-folds or normalizes them, so two spellings that differ in
any byte name two different attributes.

The `loonfs.` prefix is reserved for system-owned attributes. This
type accepts a reserved key, because a durable row has to be able to
carry a system attribute. The write operation is where a caller's
attempt to write a reserved key is rejected.

AttributeRevisionNo.description:
Monotonically increasing attribute revision counter within one inode.

Every inode starts at revision 0 with an empty attribute map, and every
effective update — one that changes the map — advances the counter by
one. The counter is the optimistic-concurrency token for attribute
writes: a writer states the revision it expects, and the write fails
when the inode has moved past it. The counter is not an index into a
history. LoonFS keeps the current map and this number, and promises no
queryable record of earlier maps.

AttributeValue.description:
One validated attribute value.

A value is at most [`MAX_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_BYTES`] UTF-8 bytes. It is
otherwise free text: control characters and the empty string are legal.
Empty is a stored value, not a tombstone; only an explicit remove
operation deletes an attribute.

Attributes.description:
A validated attribute map for one inode.

Construction and decoding both enforce the same limits: a map holds at
most [`MAX_ATTRIBUTE_ENTRIES`] entries, each value is at most
[`MAX_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_BYTES`] UTF-8 bytes, and the whole map is at most
[`MAX_ATTRIBUTES_TOTAL_BYTES`] logical UTF-8 bytes. The total counts key
bytes and value bytes and nothing else, so it does not depend on the
encoding the map is written in. Durable state that breaks a limit fails to
decode rather than decoding to something smaller.

An empty map is valid. It is the cleared state, and clearing an inode's
attributes is a real update with its own revision.

AttributesProjection.description: One inode's structurally complete attribute projection.

attributes.description:
The complete attribute map at `attributes_revision_no`.

An inode that has never had attributes written is at revision 0 with
an empty map.

attributes_revision_no.description: The attribute revision this projection represents.

attributes_updated_at_ms.description:
Time of the latest attribute update, in Unix milliseconds. This is
`None` for the initial empty state at revision 0.

oneOf.description:
Actor responsible for the latest attribute update. This is `None` for
the initial empty state at revision 0.

allOf.description: File-or-directory classification and its kind-specific payload.

oneOf.description: The inode's attribute projection, when requested.

absolute_path.description: Absolute path as rendered from stored display names.

created_at_ms.description:
Time the inode was created, in Unix milliseconds. Sequence numbers
determine order.

created_by.description: Actor that created this inode, as supplied by the application.

oneOf.description: Stored display name for this path component, absent for the nameless root.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence this answer was read from.

inode_id.description: Stable inode identity for this item.

oneOf.description: Parent directory inode, or `None` for the root.

AuthoritativePathEntry.description:
Authoritative metadata for one visible path.

This is the result shape for stat/list style reads. The entry kind carries
the file-only revision and content summary, so a directory cannot carry a
partial file payload. Attributes are likewise projected as one value or
omitted as one value, while serializing as prefixed sibling fields.
The attribute revision is read independently — clients feed it to
`expected_attributes_revision_no` on the next write without touching the
values — so this is a prefixed-sibling projection rather than a value
consumed as one nested unit.

oneOf.title: AuthoritativePathEntryDirectory
oneOf.description:
A directory, which has no revision payload in v0.

The entry tag reuses [`InodeKind`]'s wire vocabulary.

oneOf.title: AuthoritativePathEntryFile
oneOf.description: A file and its current revision summary.

committed_at_ms.description:
Time of the current revision, in Unix milliseconds. Revision
sequences determine order.

revision_actor.description: Actor responsible for the current revision.

size_bytes.description:
Current file size in bytes.

This remains explicit even though `content_ref` also carries the
length because callers sort directory listings by this field.

AuthoritativePathEntryKind.description: Kind-specific metadata for an authoritative path entry.

BeginDownloadRequest.description:
What a client names when it asks to read a file directly.

A path and, optionally, the revision it wants — the same two things the
proxied content read takes, so a caller switching transports changes
nothing about what it is asking for.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to read.

oneOf.description: Revision to read, or `None` for the path's current revision.

BeginDownloadResponse.description:
A short-lived capability to read one file's content object, plus
everything the reader needs to check what arrives.

The raw object key is deliberately not here, exactly as it is not in a
`direct_put` grant: a client learns a URL that expires, not an address it
can revisit.

The grant names one immutable content object, so it does not go stale
when the path moves on. A commit that replaces the file writes a new
object and leaves this one alone; what the capability reads is what the
requested revision held when the grant was issued, and the reference
says which bytes those are.

absolute_path.description: Absolute path as rendered from stored display names.

access.description: Short-lived read capability the client uses without learning the raw object key.

content_ref.description:
Identity, byte length, and checksum evidence for the object the
capability reads. A reader checks the bytes it receives against
`size_bytes` and recomputes `checksum.algorithm` over the complete
payload.

revision_no.description: Revision the capability reads, resolved from the request.

oneOf.title: BeginUploadServiceProxied
oneOf.description: Send the bytes to the service, which writes the content object.

oneOf.title: BeginUploadDirectPut
oneOf.description:
Write the whole object through one presigned request. The server
signs exactly these bytes into the write it authorizes, so the claim
is required.

content.description: Byte length and digest of the payload about to be written.

oneOf.title: BeginUploadDirectMultipart
oneOf.description: Write the object in parts through presigned part uploads.

Selects the part geometry; absent takes the server's default.
A multipart upload claims its content at completion, so nothing
about the payload is declared here.

BeginUploadRequest.description:
Request to start an upload session, tagged by transport mode.

Each variant contains only fields valid for that transport, so invalid
combinations are rejected during decoding. The `mode` field is required.

oneOf.title: BeginUploadResponseServiceProxied
oneOf.description: The service will receive the bytes and write the content object.

namespace_id.description: Namespace authorized to consume the eventual staged content.

upload_id.description:
Durable session identity used by subsequent append and completion
calls.

oneOf.title: BeginUploadResponseDirectPut
oneOf.description: One presigned request writes the whole object.

direct_put.description: The object this session writes, and the capability to write it.

namespace_id.description: Namespace authorized to consume the eventual staged content.

upload_id.description: Durable session identity used by subsequent completion calls.

oneOf.title: BeginUploadResponseDirectMultipart
oneOf.description: Presigned part uploads assemble the object.

direct_multipart.description: The geometry the client cuts its payload to.

namespace_id.description: Namespace authorized to consume the eventual staged content.

upload_id.description:
Durable session identity used by subsequent part-signing and
completion calls.

BeginUploadResponse.description:
Response to starting an upload session, tagged by transport mode.

Each variant contains only the fields needed by that transport. Unknown
response fields are accepted for forward compatibility.

CapabilityDocument.description:
A deployment's self-description (API spec, "Capability discovery").

A remote client fetches this from `GET /v0/capabilities` and caches it; an
embedded engine exposes the same document as a constant. SDK gating logic
is therefore identical for both backends: check [`supports`] or
[`has_profile`], and treat a `not_supported` error as authoritative when
the two disagree.

[`supports`]: CapabilityDocument::supports
[`has_profile`]: CapabilityDocument::has_profile

features.description:
Named features and whether this deployment supports them. An absent
key means unsupported.

limits.description: Advisory numeric limits clients may use to pre-validate requests.

profiles.description:
Advertised profiles, each `plane/version`. All-or-nothing: every
required op of an advertised profile is implemented.

ChangeSeq.description:
Monotonically increasing namespace commit sequence number.

This is the global visibility order for a namespace.

after_seq.description: Exclusive cursor supplied by the caller, or the endpoint's initial position.

changes.description: Logical commits after `after_seq`, ordered by ascending namespace sequence.

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose ordered commit stream was read.

oneOf.description: Cursor to request when another page remains, or `None` at `through_seq`.

through_seq.description: Snapshot head through which this page was evaluated.

CheckpointId.description:
Durable checkpoint identifier.

A checkpoint is a durable bookmark to a namespace manifest version.

oneOf.title: CheckpointOwnerUser
oneOf.description: An operator-created pin, released by id or by its own expiry.

name.description:
The label the creator recorded. Not a key: several records may
carry one label over different bases.

oneOf.title: CheckpointOwnerFork
oneOf.description:
A fork target keeping its source basis alive for the length of one
fork attempt.

target_namespace_id.description: Namespace whose continued existence keeps this pin standing.

CheckpointOwnerSummary.description:
Who a checkpoint record answers to, as the record durably records it.

The two owners have different releases, so a listing that names the
owner also says which records the release endpoint will act on: a user
pin is released by id, and a fork lease is released by deleting the
target namespace it protects.

CheckpointSummary.description: One active checkpoint record, reported from what the record carries.

checkpoint_id.description:
Durable checkpoint id, as the creation response returned it. This is
what the release endpoint takes.

checkpoint_seq.description:
Sequence the pinned basis covers — the same number the creation
response reported as `checkpoint_seq`.

created_at_ms.description: When the record was written, in Unix milliseconds.

expires_at_ms.description:
When garbage collection may release the record without being asked,
in Unix milliseconds. Absent means the pin holds until it is
released. An instant already in the past is a record whose expiry
has passed and which no collection pass has reached yet: it is still
a root, so it is still listed.

owner.description: Who the record answers to, and the label a user pin carries.

Checksum.description:
An algorithm and its canonical lowercase-hex checksum value.

The enclosing value defines which bytes the checksum covers.

value.description:
Lowercase hex of the raw checksum bytes.

The algorithm is its own field, so the value carries no prefix.
Provider APIs that report base64 are converted at the adapter.

ChecksumAlgorithm.description:
Supported checksum algorithms.

The enclosing value defines which bytes a checksum covers. Unknown
algorithms fail to decode because every in-memory `ChecksumAlgorithm` must
be recomputable by this build. Adding a variant also requires adding its
implementation.

CommitId.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key for one logical commit.

Reuse the same `CommitId` when retrying the same request. The accepted
grammar is 1 to 128 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores,
or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. [`CommitId::generate`] mints
`c_<32 lowercase hex>`, but callers may supply any value in that grammar.

CommitRequest.description:
A request to commit one or more filesystem operations.

Operations run in order and either all succeed or none are committed. A
request with one operation uses the same fingerprint rules as a batch.

Unknown fields are rejected here for the same reason they are on
[`FilesystemOperation`]: the fields a typo can hide are the ones that
decide whether the commit is guarded at all.

actor.description: Actor responsible for the commit, as supplied by the application.

commit_id.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key for the whole request.

content_tokens.description:
Proofs for any new external content refs introduced by this request.
One proof covers every operation that names its content ref.

message.description:
Caller annotation recorded on the commit and reported by the change
feed. Part of the commit's identity: reusing `commit_id` with a
different message is a `commit_id_reuse_conflict`, exactly as it is
for an explicit commit.

operations.description:
Ordered operations to apply. Must be non-empty; they commit all
together or not at all.

CommitResponse.description:
Result of one commit.

Every commit resolves to this envelope — path-oriented operations and
explicit commits, embedded or remote. The commit id is the caller's
reconciliation handle: resubmitting the same request with the same id
replays this result instead of committing twice.

commit_id.description:
Idempotency key the commit landed under: caller-supplied, or
generated on the caller's behalf when the request carried none.

committed_seq.description: Sequence number where the commit became visible.

CommittedChange.description: One committed change in namespace order.

actor.description: Actor responsible for the commit, as supplied by the application.

commit_id.description: Client idempotency key for this logical commit.

committed_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock stamp of the commit, in Unix milliseconds.
Observational: `committed_seq` is the order.

committed_seq.description: Namespace sequence for this logical commit.

events.description:
Semantic filesystem events for this commit, in the order the commit
applied them. One request operation may produce more than one event
(see [`FilesystemChange`]).

message.description: Caller annotation, omitted when absent and carrying no filesystem semantics.

oneOf.title: CompleteUploadContentRef
oneOf.description:
Completes a session the server named a content object for: the
caller names it back and the server proves the object matches.

content_ref.description:
Content identity the caller expects the session to have settled
on.

oneOf.title: CompleteUploadMultipart
oneOf.description: Completes a `direct_multipart` session with what it uploaded.

content.description:
The assembled object's length and checksum, which completion
verifies against the provider's own reading of the object.

parts.description:
Every part the client uploaded, in ascending part order. The
server holds no part records of its own, so this list is what it
assembles the object from.

CompleteUploadRequest.description:
Request to complete an upload.

A service-proxied or `direct_put` session receives its content reference
before the upload and returns that reference at completion. A
`direct_multipart` session instead provides the completed parts and a
claim describing the assembled object.

The variants share no fields, so fields from one completion type are
rejected when used with the other type. The server also checks that the
completion type matches the transport stored in the upload session.

CompleteUploadResponse.description: Response after an upload session is completed.

content_ref.description: Verified immutable content selected by the completed session.

namespace_id.description: Namespace that owns the completed session.

upload_id.description: Session whose result is now frozen for idempotent completion retries.

validated_content_token.description: Opaque server proof for a later commit, or `None` when the backend needs no token.

CompletedUploadPart.description:
One uploaded part, as the client observed the provider accept it.

The server keeps no durable record of any part. Part bookkeeping is the
client's, exactly as it is in the provider's own multipart API, and this
is where the client hands it back.

checksum.description: Checksum the part was signed and accepted with.

etag.description: Entity tag the provider returned for the accepted part.

ContentId.description:
Durable identity of one immutable content object.

The body is 128 fully random bits, with no time component: content
object keys shard on the id's leading characters, and a clock-derived
prefix would put every upload in one window into one shard. The id
names *which object*, never what it contains — integrity evidence
rides [`crate::ContentRef`] beside it.

ContentRef.description:
Pointer to one immutable content object.

`content_id` is identity — *which* object — and the checksum is
evidence about its bytes. Separating the two is what lets the final
object key exist before the first byte is read.

A `ContentRef` is safe to publish only after the referenced bytes are
durable in the namespace's content store.

checksum.description: Mandatory checksum over the complete object.

content_id.description: Immutable identity of the referenced object.

kind.description: Content strategy used by the referenced object.

size_bytes.description: Complete byte length of the referenced content.

CreateCheckpointRequest.description: Request to create a durable checkpoint pin.

name.description:
Label recorded on the checkpoint record. A label, not a key: several
records may carry the same name over different bases.

ttl_ms.description:
Optional lifetime; the server computes the record's expiry from its
own clock. Absent means the pin holds until explicitly released.

oneOf.description: Manifest `metadata/root.json` references after the operation.

expires_at_ms.description: Expiry recorded on the record, when the request carried a `ttl_ms`.

DeleteDirectoryBehavior.description: Directory delete behavior for path-oriented deletes.

head_seq.description:
The head's last committed sequence; the delete linearized
immediately after it, so this is where history ended.

DeletedDirentry.description:
Directory binding removed by a path deletion.

Tombstones retain this binding after the corresponding unbind row may be
collected. Undelete uses it to restore the original parent and name.

name_key.description: Canonical key the binding was reachable under.

DestinationBehavior.description: Destination-conflict behavior for path-oriented puts, moves, and copies.

DirectMultipartUpload.description:
Part geometry returned for a direct multipart upload.

The begin response does not include a content reference or part count
because the final payload is not known yet. The server owns the provider
upload id and returns the content reference only after completion.

checksum_algorithm.description:
Checksum algorithm every part and the complete assembled payload must
use for this session.

part_size_bytes.description:
Byte length of every part except the last. At most 10,000 parts may
be uploaded, so this bounds the object at `part_size_bytes × 10_000`.

DirectMultipartUploadOptions.description:
What a `direct_multipart` client asks for when it opens a session.

A begin request declares no length and no digest: the session exists to
receive bytes whose length may not be known yet. All it settles is the
geometry the client cuts to.

part_size_bytes.description:
Byte length of every part except the last, or `None` for the
server's default.

The value bounds the object: a provider accepts at most 10,000
parts, so this session can carry at most `part_size_bytes × 10_000`
bytes. A client that knows its payload is very large asks for a
larger part size; one that does not know its length at all takes the
default and keeps asking for part URLs until its stream ends.

DirectPutUpload.description: Presigned direct_put upload details. The raw object key is intentionally not public.

access.description: Short-lived write capability the client uses without learning the raw object key.

content_ref.description:
Immutable object identity the server minted, plus the byte length and
checksum covered by the signed request. Completion and the later
commit both name exactly this reference.

DisableGrepIndexResponse.description: Result of disabling the grep index on a namespace (admin plane).

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose grep root was disabled.

was_enabled.description: False when the namespace had no enabled grep root.

DisplayName.description: User-facing spelling of one path component.

EnableGrepIndexResponse.description: Result of enabling the grep index on a namespace (admin plane).

already_enabled.description: True when the namespace already carried an enabled grep root.

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose grep root was enabled.

state.description: The durable lifecycle this call published or found.

ErrorDetails.description:
Optional machine-readable details for an [`ApiError`].

Clients make retry decisions from the error code and use these fields for
relevant identifiers such as commit ids, writer epochs, and revisions.
Fields may be absent and clients must ignore fields they do not use.

active_acquired_at_ms.description:
Unix milliseconds at which the current epoch's acquirer took it, when
the head recorded one. Writer ids are process labels, so two runs on
one machine can share one; the stamp is what tells them apart.

oneOf.description: Deletion generation actually active for the inode.

active_writer.description:
Writer id recorded by the current epoch's acquirer, when the head
recorded one.

oneOf.description: Epoch that currently owns the namespace.
Attribute revision that is actually current for the inode.

Head sequence the namespace was actually at, which is what a caller
that still means to delete it retries against.
Revision that is actually current; absent when the inode has none.
Change-feed cursor the request asked to resume after.
Idempotency key of the commit the error concerns.

committed_fingerprint.description:
Semantic identity of the mutation that already landed under that
commit id, from the same receipt as `committed_seq` and present
exactly when it is. A retry recomputes this value from the request it
just made — see
[`put_retry_fingerprint`](crate::put_retry_fingerprint) — and equality
is what proves the two are the same request.

oneOf.description:
Sequence at which that commit id already landed. Present when the
failure was decided against a durable commit receipt, which is what
holds the sequence; absent when nothing has committed under the id
yet and two live requests are simply claiming it at once.
Attribute revision the request expected to be current.

Head sequence a namespace delete required the namespace to still be
at.
Revision the request expected to be current.
Epoch the failing writer session held when it was displaced.
Inode the failed precondition or operation targeted.

operation_index.description:
Position, in the request's operation list, of the operation that
failed. A commit applies all of its operations or none of them, so
this names the one that stopped the whole request.

oneOf.description: Deletion generation an undelete asked to recover.
Oldest sequence still promised for incremental replay.

actor.description: Actor responsible for this revision, as supplied by the application.

committed_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock stamp of the commit that created this revision, in Unix
milliseconds. Observational: `committed_seq` is the order.

committed_seq.description: Namespace sequence that created this revision.

inode_id.description: File inode that owns this revision.

revision_no.description: Revision number within the file inode.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeCreated
oneOf.description: A file or directory was created.
Content of the first revision, for file creations.

display_name.description: User-facing spelling of the new entry.

parent_inode_id.description: Directory the new entry was bound under.

oneOf.description: First revision number, for file creations.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeContentChanged
oneOf.description:
A file received a new current revision — a put over an existing
file, or a revision restore (one durable fact for both).

content_ref.description: Immutable content published by the revision.

revision_no.description: New monotonic position in that file's revision history.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeMoved
oneOf.description: An inode moved to a new parent directory or name.

from_parent_inode_id.description: Directory that held the old binding.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeDeleted
oneOf.description:
A file or directory subtree was deleted. The enclosing change's
`committed_seq` is the deletion generation an undelete request passes
as `deleted_at_seq`.

Directory binding removed by the deletion, when the delete
recorded one.

inode_id.description: Inode at the root of the deleted subtree.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeUndeleted
oneOf.description: A deleted inode was recovered and re-bound.

parent_inode_id.description: Directory the recovered entry was bound under.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeAttributesChanged
oneOf.description: An inode's attributes changed.

attributes.description:
The inode's complete attribute map after the update, so a consumer
projects it without reading anything back. An empty map is the
cleared state.

attributes_revision_no.description: New attribute revision for that inode.

FilesystemChange.description:
One semantic filesystem change inside a commit.

A commit's events are the operations it applied, in the order it applied
them. One request operation can apply several: creating missing parent
directories, or replacing a file by moving over it, each produce an event
per directory created or file replaced. So a request with three
operations may report more than three events, and the events stay in
request order. Events name inodes and their parent-directory bindings
rather than full paths; a consumer that needs paths can stat the inode or
maintain its own binding projection from this feed.

oneOf.title: FsOpCreateDirectory
oneOf.description: Create one directory.

parents.description:
Also create missing ancestor directories (the same auto-create
`put_file` performs). The final component must still be new.

path.description: Absolute destination path, rejected when invalid or already bound.

oneOf.title: FsOpPutFile
oneOf.description: Create or replace one file with an already-durable content ref.

behavior.description: Whether an existing file may receive a new revision instead of causing a conflict.

content_ref.description: Immutable bytes that must be covered by a valid preparation proof.

oneOf.description:
When set (with `replace` behavior), the put applies only while
the file's current revision is still this one; a raced write
fails the request instead of silently stacking on it, and a
missing file answers `path_not_found`.

path.description: Absolute destination path; missing ancestors are created automatically.

oneOf.title: FsOpDeletePath
oneOf.description: Delete one path.

behavior.description: Whether a non-empty directory may be tombstoned recursively.

oneOf.description:
When set, the delete applies only if the path still resolves to
this inode; a raced rebinding fails the request instead of
deleting (and reporting a recovery handle for) the wrong inode.

path.description: Absolute path that must resolve to a visible inode.

oneOf.title: FsOpMovePath
oneOf.description: Move one path to another path.

behavior.description: Whether an existing destination file may be replaced.

from_path.description: Absolute source path that must resolve to a visible inode.

to_path.description: Absolute destination whose parent must be visible and writable.

oneOf.title: FsOpCopyPath
oneOf.description: Copy one file path to another path.

behavior.description: Whether an existing destination file may receive a copied revision.

from_path.description: Absolute source path that must resolve to a visible file.

to_path.description: Absolute destination whose parent must be visible and writable.

oneOf.title: FsOpUndelete
oneOf.description:
Recover a deleted file or subtree: revoke the deletion of
`inode_id` recorded at `deleted_at_seq` (both reported by the
delete and by the change feed) and re-bind it. Answers
`not_deleted` when that generation is not the live one, so a stale
request never cancels a later delete.

deleted_at_seq.description: Observed deletion sequence, which prevents cancelling a newer tombstone generation.

inode_id.description: Deleted inode to make reachable again.

oneOf.description:
Optional destination for the restored inode.

When absent, the inode is rebound to the parent and name recorded by the
deletion. Parent identity, rather than an old path string, keeps this
correct after ancestor renames. An explicit path is required when the
deletion recorded no binding.

oneOf.title: FsOpRestoreRevision
oneOf.description: Restore an older revision as the current revision for a path.

path.description: Absolute path that must resolve to a visible file.

source_revision_no.description: Existing historical revision whose content will be copied into a new current revision.

oneOf.title: FsOpUpdateAttributes
oneOf.description: Write and remove attributes on the inode one path resolves to.

When set, the update applies only while the inode's attribute
revision is still this one. Absent means the update is applied
over whatever revision is current; either way the write carries
its own revision guard, so a concurrent update never merges
silently.

When set, the update applies only if the path still resolves to
this inode; a raced rebinding fails the request instead of
writing attributes onto the wrong inode.

path.description: Absolute path that must resolve to a visible file or directory.

remove.description:
Attribute keys to remove.

A list preserves duplicate entries so validation can report them instead
of silently deduplicating the request.

set.description:
Attributes to write. Each key replaces whatever the inode
currently holds under it; keys the inode holds and this map does
not name are left alone.

propertyNames.description:
Validated name of one inode attribute.

A key is 1 to 128 UTF-8 bytes and carries no Unicode control
character, which is also what rejects NUL. Keys are compared exactly:
nothing case-folds or normalizes them, so two spellings that differ in
any byte name two different attributes.

The `loonfs.` prefix is reserved for system-owned attributes. This
type accepts a reserved key, because a durable row has to be able to
carry a system attribute. The write operation is where a caller's
attempt to write a reserved key is rejected.

FilesystemOperation.description:
One path-oriented filesystem operation.

Unknown fields are rejected because concurrency guards are optional. A
misspelled guard must fail decoding instead of silently becoming `None`
and allowing an unguarded write. Any future fieldless variant must use
empty braces so serde also rejects unexpected fields for that variant.

new_namespace_id.description: Durable namespace id for the fork target.

GcRequest.description:
Optional overrides for one garbage-collection pass. Absent fields use
the server's conservative defaults.

Every field is optional, so a typo would take the default instead of the
override the caller asked for. Unknown fields are rejected so a misspelled
`max_objects` fails loudly rather than running an unbounded pass.

cursor.description:
Opaque resume token returned as `next_cursor` by an earlier pass
against the same namespace.

grace_window_ms.description:
Objects younger than this are never deleted, reachable or not. The
window has a derived safety floor (publication budgets plus provider
deadlines); a smaller value is rejected as `invalid_request`.

max_objects.description:
Maximum objects this invocation may read or decide. Omit to retain
the run-to-completion behavior.

A completed upload session past its reclamation grace makes the pass
read every live manifest and retained WAL segment to find out
whether anything still references its content, and that read is
charged here like any other. A budget too small to finish it does
not stall the pass: the session is retained, the response sets
`content_reclamation_deferred`, and the sweep carries on through
everything else. What a chronically small budget costs is content
left unreclaimed, not progress. Give a pass at least as many objects
as the namespace has live manifests and retained segments for that
content to come back.

GcResponse.description: Result of one mark-and-sweep garbage-collection pass.

budget_exhausted.description:
True when the pass stopped because `max_objects` ran out before it
finished. Whatever it did before that is reported here and stands;
rerun with the returned cursor, or with a larger budget, to
continue. A budget too small for the namespace's own roots stops a
pass before it decides anything at all, which is what this says and
an empty report on its own does not.

content_reclamation_deferred.description:
True when the pass skipped completed-content reclamation because
what it needs — the namespace's live roots, then the reference
collection over them — did not fit in `max_objects`. Nothing was
ever decided from a partial collection; a later pass with room for
the whole scan reclaims what this one left behind. A pass that had
room for the roots swept every other candidate normally around the
skip, and one that did not also reports `budget_exhausted`.

degraded_retention.description: True when ambiguous roots suppressed manifest/table deletion.

deleted_checkpoint_records.description: Released checkpoint records deleted after their grace window.

deleted_content_objects.description:
Content objects reclaimed because their upload session completed,
aged past the derived reclamation grace, and nothing the namespace
can reach references them. The upload half's cleanup of abandoned
sessions is not counted here: it deletes unconditionally, whether or
not the session ever wrote anything.

deleted_upload_sessions.description: Upload-session control objects deleted after the reap window.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque resume token when more candidates remain. Resuming rebuilds
every safety proof; the token carries enumeration position only and
is valid only against the same namespace.

next_reclamation_at_ms.description:
The soonest instant still ahead of this pass at which something it
retained becomes reclaimable: an open session's lease plus the grace
window, an aborted session's grace, or a completed session's derived
content-reclamation grace. A scheduler reads this to decide when to
come back, so a namespace needs no other side channel to have its
reclamation happen.

It reports what this pass saw and nothing more. A pass that stopped
on `next_cursor` examined only part of the keyspace, and candidates
that age out under a plain grace window on their object timestamps
carry no deadline here at all, so absence is never a claim that
nothing is owed.

released_expired_checkpoints.description:
Checkpoint records released because their expiry passed, or because
they sit on a terminally deleted namespace.

released_fork_checkpoints.description:
Fork-owned checkpoint records released because their target namespace
is provably gone.

released_missing_basis_checkpoints.description:
Active checkpoint records released because their basis manifest is
verifiably gone.

retained.description:
The same total, split by the decision that spared each candidate.
The total above stays because it is what every existing consumer
reads; this says why.

retained_candidates.description:
Candidates retained at delete time (grace window, missing
timestamps, or reachable from the fresh root set).

GrepGcRequest.description: One explicit grep-index garbage-collection pass (admin plane).

cursor.description:
Opaque resume token returned as `next_cursor` by an earlier pass
against the same namespace.

max_objects.description:
Reads this pass may spend before returning with a `next_cursor`.
Omit to take the same per-pass default the runtime's own collection
takes.

GrepGcResponse.description: Result of one explicit grep-index garbage-collection pass (admin plane).

deleted_other_objects.description: Other unreferenced grep objects deleted after the grace window.

deleted_segments.description: Unreferenced grep segments deleted after the grace window.

namespace_degraded.description: Whether unreadable namespace or grep state forced conservative retention.

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose grep-owned keyspace was inspected.

namespace_reaped.description: Whether an absent or tombstoned namespace had extension state reaped.

next_cursor.description: Present when the budget stopped the pass with keys left to examine.

retained_candidates.description: Young or concurrently revived candidates retained by the pass.

oneOf.description: No index is maintained for this namespace.

The initial walk over a pinned checkpoint is running. Nothing is
searchable yet.

checkpoint_id.description: Checkpoint pinning the state being walked.

oneOf.description:
Inode the walk resumes strictly after. Absent before the first
page.

target_seq.description:
Namespace sequence the pinned checkpoint captured. Reaching it
is what completes the backfill.

oneOf.description:
The index follows the change feed. Commits at or below the watermark
are searchable.

built_through_seq.description: Sequence of the commit at the index cursor.

next_event_index.description:
Offset of the next change event within `built_through_seq`, or
zero when the whole commit is represented.

GrepIndexLifecycle.description:
Where a namespace's grep index is in its lifecycle.

Each phase contains only the fields valid for that phase. `Backfilling`
reports its target and current position. `Steady` reports how far the
index has been built. Clients should treat a namespace as searchable only
when the index is in the `Steady` phase.

GrepIndexStatusResponse.description:
The namespace's grep-index lifecycle and its cheap bookkeeping (admin
plane).

next_run_ordinal.description: Next logical run ordinal the index will allocate.

reorganize_pending.description: True while a partitioned segment reorganization is in progress.

state.description: Where the index is in its lifecycle.

absolute_path.description: The file's absolute path, derived at the snapshot.

byte_offset.description: Byte offset of the match within the file.

inode_id.description: Durable identity of the matched file.

line.description: The matching line, truncated to the server's line cap.

line_number.description: One-based line number of the match.

revision_no.description: The matched revision (the newest visible one at the snapshot).

GrepRequest.description:
One content-search request.

Every field but `pattern` is optional, and each one selects results. A
misspelled `case_insensitive` or `path_prefix` would decode to the default
and answer a different search than the caller asked for, with no sign that
anything was dropped, so unknown fields are rejected.

allow_scan.description:
Permit a capped exhaustive scan when the pattern yields no required
grams. Refused beyond the server's scan budget.

allow_stale.description:
When the unindexed tail exceeds the scan budget, return
indexed-only results (reported via `tail_scanned: false`) instead
of failing with `index_lagging`.

case_insensitive.description:
Match case-insensitively. Verification is exact; the index remains
consulted through its case-folded grams.

cursor.description:
Resume cursor from a previous page. The cursor resumes strictly
after the last candidate the issuing page finished scanning and is
bound to that page's request; each page is evaluated against the
namespace head at page time.

oneOf.description:
Restrict matches to files under this complete absolute path, resolved
to a directory inode before candidates are filtered.

pattern.description:
The pattern, in the Rust `regex` crate's dialect (no backreferences
or lookaround). Patterns that require no literal bytes are rejected
with `query_unindexable` unless `allow_scan` is set.

built_through_seq.description: Commits at or below this sequence were answered from the index.

head_seq.description:
Sequence this page was evaluated at. Pages are evaluated against
the namespace head at page time; the cursor is an ordering resume,
not a snapshot pin.

matches.description:
Matches in ascending `(inode_id, byte_offset)` order. A page may
return fewer matches than its limit and still carry a cursor: the
per-page verified-candidate budget bounds how much content one
request reads, whatever the plan's false-positive rate.

tail_scanned.description:
True when revisions after `built_through_seq` were scanned
exhaustively; false only when `allow_stale` skipped them.

InodeId.description:
Numeric identity of a file or directory within a namespace.

Inodes are stable across renames.

ListCheckpointsResponse.description: Every active checkpoint record a namespace currently carries.

checkpoints.description:
Active records, oldest first. Released records are absent because a
release is what stops a record pinning anything; a released record
that garbage collection has not yet deleted is not reported either.

absolute_path.description: Absolute file path requested by the caller.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence used for the read.

inode_id.description: File inode whose revisions were returned.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, if more revisions are available.

ListPathEntriesResponse.description:
One directory listing and the namespace head it was answered at.

The envelope names the listing target and head so an empty directory
still tells the caller which state it observed, and so the response can
grow without reshaping `entries`.

absolute_path.description: Absolute path of the listed directory.

entries.description:
Directory entries for this page.

Entries are returned in canonical name-key order. Higher-level display
surfaces may sort entries separately for presentation.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence this listing was read from.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, if more entries remain.

ListTrashResponse.description: One trash listing page: the namespace's recoverable deletions.

head_seq.description: Head sequence this page was evaluated at.

MaintenanceStepRequest.description:
One explicit maintenance step: the actions it selects, and nothing more.

Selection is presence. Each field names one independent action, and a
step runs exactly the ones the body carries — a request that selects
nothing is rejected rather than quietly doing nothing. Unknown fields are
rejected for the same reason: a misspelled selector would leave its action
unrun, and the caller would read the empty report as "there was nothing to
do".

advance_retention.description:
Advance the retention floor to the flushed manifest head. Nothing
surrenders replay history unless this is true.

oneOf.description:
Run one bounded mark-and-sweep garbage-collection pass. Nothing
sweeps unless this is present.

Fold the visible WAL tail into metadata tables and merge one bounded
reorganization unit. The two travel together: folding a tail is what
creates the delta runs a reorganization merges.

MaintenanceStepResponse.description:
Result of one explicit maintenance step.

One report per action the request selected, and none for an action it
did not: an absent field means "not selected", never "ran and found
nothing to do". The latter is what the outcomes inside a report say.

oneOf.description: What the collection pass reclaimed.
What the metadata-upkeep action did.
Where the retention floor ended up.

status_before.description: Namespace status observed before the step acted.

ManifestId.description:
Monotonically increasing namespace manifest identity.

This is the durable file-set version identity for namespace manifests.
Initial/fork manifests may be seeded from the current head sequence, but
later manifest ids can advance for checkpoint metadata, compaction, or
fork/index metadata without a new namespace commit.

max_wal_tail_segments.description:
Flush the visible WAL tail once it reaches this many segments.
Absent uses the server's default threshold; zero, and any value above
the write-rejection threshold, are rejected as `invalid_request`.

MetadataMaintenanceResponse.description: What one metadata-upkeep action did, part by part.

NameKey.description:
Name-policy-derived directory entry key.

Use this for exact name preconditions. Keep user-facing spelling in
`DisplayName`.

NamespaceId.description:
Durable id for one namespace.

A namespace is one filesystem history. This id is not a display name and
should not be reused after destruction. Its serialized form is 1 to 128
lowercase ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens, starting
with a letter or digit; the `loonfs-` prefix is reserved for system use.

NamespaceStatusResponse.description:
Status summary for one namespace.

This is the point-lookup answer to "does this namespace exist, and where
is its head?" — cheaper than listing all namespaces when only one matters.

oneOf.description: Current manifest pointer recorded by the head.

retention_floor_seq.description: Oldest sequence still promised for incremental replay.

wal_tail_segments.description: Number of visible WAL segments after the current manifest.

NamespaceSummary.description: Short namespace identifier returned by namespace create/fork operations.

oneOf.title: ObjectTransferAccessPresignedUrl
oneOf.description: Short-lived URL plus required headers for one object-store write.

headers.description: Headers that are covered by the signature and must be sent.

method.description: HTTP method the client must use.

ReleaseCheckpointResponse.description: Result of releasing a checkpoint pin.

was_active.description:
True when this call flipped an active record to released; false when
the record was already released or no longer exists. Release is
idempotent — the end state is the same either way.

ReorganizeStepOutcome.description:
What the metadata-reorganization part of a maintenance step did.

Deliberately coarse: the run counts and byte budgets a reorganization
consumes are engine policy, not a wire contract.

RetainedCandidates.description:
Why a pass kept what it kept: `retained_candidates` split by the
decision that spared each candidate.

The reasons are a closed set — one per place the sweep decides against
deleting — so every field is always reported, and a zero is the answer
that nothing was kept for that reason. The counts sum to
`retained_candidates`.

Retention is a decision per candidate examined, not per object in the
namespace: one object examined by two passes is counted by each.

checkpoint_not_releasable.description:
A checkpoint record this pass could have advanced but could not
prove ready: a lost compare-and-swap, an unreadable record, a fork
target not provably gone, a released record still inside its grace
window, or an active pin that is simply doing its job. The pins
themselves are listed by
`GET /v0/admin/namespaces/{ns}/checkpoints`.

content_scan_deferred.description:
A completed session whose content reclamation was skipped because
the reference scan did not fit in `max_objects`
(`content_reclamation_deferred` is set too).

degraded_roots.description:
Root resolution failed somewhere in this pass, so manifest and table
deletion was suppressed wholesale (`degraded_retention` is set too).

grace_window.description:
Unreachable, but younger than the grace window by the object's own
provider timestamp. A later pass deletes it.

no_provider_timestamp.description:
Unreachable, and the provider reported no last-modified time at all,
so the object's age is unknown and it is treated as young.

no_reference_manifest.description:
Unreachable, but this namespace published no manifest old enough to
say what it referenced when the grace window opened, so nothing
proves the object was already unreferenced then. A reader that pinned
its anchor inside the window may still be reading it, and the pass
keeps it until a manifest ages past the window.

referenced.description:
Selected as unreachable, then found reachable by the re-verification
that runs immediately before every deletion. A candidate the pass
already knew was reachable is never examined at all, so this counts
the namespace moving underneath the pass rather than the size of its
live set.

unrecognized_key.description:
A key under a swept family that this collector does not recognize as
one of its own. Never deleted, whatever its age.

upload_session_undecided.description:
An upload session held over for a reason no clock resolves: a lost
compare-and-swap, a record that vanished mid-pass, or a reference
set this pass could not establish. Only a later pass answers it.

upload_session_window.description:
An upload session waiting out a window a clock resolves: an open
session's lease plus the grace, an aborted session's grace, or a
completed session's derived content-reclamation grace.
`next_reclamation_at_ms` reports the soonest of these.

RevisionNo.description: Monotonically increasing file revision counter within one file inode.

SignUploadPartsRequest.description: Request for part-upload capabilities on an open multipart session.

parts.description:
Parts to authorize, each with the checksum the provider will enforce
on it. Asking again for a part already uploaded is how a client
retries one: a repeated part is last-write-wins at the provider.

SignUploadPartsResponse.description: Response carrying one capability per requested part.

namespace_id.description: Namespace that owns the upload session.

parts.description: Capabilities in the order the request asked for them.

access.description: Short-lived write capability for that part.

StoreProbeCheckOutcome.description: What one contract check concluded about the store.

StoreProbeCheckResult.description: One named contract check and what the store did with it.

message.description:
What was expected and what happened instead. Present only on
`failed`.

StoreProbeRequest.description:
Options for one store contract probe. Empty today; a body is still sent
so later options do not change the shape of the request. An option this
build does not know is rejected rather than ignored, so a caller never
believes it selected something.

StoreProbeResponse.description: What one store contract probe observed, check by check.

checks.description:
Every check the run performed, in the order it performed them. A
failed check lives here rather than in an error: the probe answered
the question, and the answer is that the store is wrong.

run_id.description:
Label the server minted for this run. It scopes the objects the run
wrote, so it identifies the run in provider logs too.

TrashEntry.description:
One recoverable deletion: an active subtree tombstone plus the identity
of the binding it deleted, when the delete recorded one. Entries with no
recorded name predate the enriched tombstone rows; their inode and
sequence still form a complete `undelete` handle.

deleted_at_ms.description: Time of the deletion, in Unix milliseconds.

deleted_at_seq.description: Commit sequence of the deletion; the other half of the handle.

oneOf.description: User-facing spelling of the deleted binding, when recorded.
Canonical key of the deleted binding, when recorded.
Directory that held the deleted binding, when recorded.

root_inode_id.description: Root inode the deletion hid; half of the recovery handle.

UploadContentClaim.description:
What an upload client claims about a complete payload.

The server mints the content object's identity — a client cannot name a
key it has not been given — so a direct upload declares only what it can
know about its own bytes. Direct PUT binds the claim into the provider
write; multipart verifies it against the assembled object at completion.

The digest names its own algorithm because providers do not agree on one:
each binds into a presigned write whatever its API can enforce. The
deployment advertises which it is, and a claim in any other algorithm is
refused at begin rather than signed into a write the provider would
reject.

checksum.description: Whole-payload checksum in the algorithm required by this operation.

size_bytes.description: Complete byte length the client will write.

UploadContentResponse.description: Response after uploading bytes into a session.

content_ref.description: Digest and byte length computed from the accepted body.

namespace_id.description: Namespace that owns the upload session.

upload_id.description: Session into which the service staged these bytes.

UploadId.description: Durable id for one upload session.

UploadPartChecksumClaim.description:
One part's checksum, supplied by the client so the server can sign it
into that part's upload URL.

part_number.description: One-based part number, at most the provider's 10,000-part limit.

oneOf.title: UploadSessionStatusOpen
oneOf.description: Accepting content until its lease passes.

expires_at_ms.description:
Unix-millisecond instant after which the session is abandoned and
may be aborted by server-side cleanup.

oneOf.title: UploadSessionStatusCompleted
oneOf.description: Final: the content is durable and verified.

content_ref.description: Verified immutable content this session settled on.

validated_content_token.description:
Freshly minted proof for a following commit, or `None` once the
session has stopped minting them.

oneOf.title: UploadSessionStatusAborted
oneOf.description: Final: the session selected no content and its object is gone.

UploadSessionStatus.description:
Observed state of an upload session.

A session starts as `Open` and ends as either `Completed` or `Aborted`.
Both final states are permanent. Reading a completed session issues a new
receipt for the durable content, so a lost commit response does not require
the content to be uploaded again.

UploadStatusResponse.description: Response for reading one upload session.

status.description: The session's state, with a fresh receipt when it is completed.

ValidatedContentToken.description:
Stateless proof that a LoonFS server already validated a content ref.

This travels in a commit request, so it decodes under the request rule:
unknown fields are rejected.

content_ref.description: Content identity the server attests it already verified.

token.description: Opaque, server-signed token. Clients must not parse it.

oneOf.description: The tail was below the threshold, so there was nothing to fold.
The step flushed the WAL tail and advanced the metadata root.

manifest_head_seq.description: Sequence covered by the published manifest.

oneOf.description:
The root already covered the attempted sequence — another publisher
got there first.

attempted_seq.description: Sequence this step attempted to flush through.

oneOf.description: A concurrent head update won the race.

observed_head_seq.description: Head sequence observed before the advance attempt.

WalFlushStepOutcome.description: What the WAL-flush part of a maintenance step did.

WriterEpoch.description: Monotonically increasing writer epoch for namespace write fencing.

DeadlineExceededResponse.description: The request exceeded `request_deadline_ms`. A timed-out mutation may still complete, so clients must determine its outcome before retrying.

schema.description: HTTP error body used by LoonFS APIs.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable reason from the [`ErrorCode`](crate::ErrorCode)
registry.

Carried as a string so clients keep working when a newer server
introduces a code they do not know; use
[`ErrorCode::parse`](crate::ErrorCode::parse) for typed access.

oneOf.description:
Structured context for the code, present when the failure carries
machine-usable identity (API spec, "Standard error contract"). Boxed
so the rare detailed error does not widen every error-carrying result.

feature.description:
For `not_supported` errors, the capability-document feature key the
client should reconcile against.

request_id.description:
Correlation id the server assigned to the failed request; the same
value is sent as the `x-request-id` response header.

bearer_auth.description: The deployment's `auth_token`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A server configured without a token accepts every request; one configured with a token answers 401 `unauthorized` without it.
